They vary in age and build (a shaved head, a grey-bearded older man, a heavyset man) and wear grey, brown and off-white rags; only Nagoji wears ochre. At the top of the stair the door stands open and torchlight spills down it. João stands there, the biggest man in the frame, bareheaded and ruddy, brown leather jerkin over a cream shirt, iron key ring at his wide belt. Behind him are three Portuguese gaol guards in dented steel morion helmets or broad black hats, loose off-white shirts, buff leather jerkins and dark breeches, with short swords and wooden clubs; no uniform coat, nothing red or blue. Nagoji in the foreground, three-quarter back view, head already lifted. Nagoji per the captivity sheet: torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged hands and wrists, ankle irons, barefoot, long curly hair loose, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble at most, small gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They woke us under cover of bells.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I counted the strokes.

copy.speaker: JOÃO
copy.text: Up! Those marked go to the docks.

panels.description: João working down the line, a leather strip held up in one hand, notched along one edge (notches only, no letters or symbols). He taps one man with it, skips two, cuffs a sleeper awake with the back of his hand. Lips pursed, humming, head tipped to a beat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The same hymn the bells had played.

panels.description: João looking down at Nagoji, his back squarely to the tally scratches on the wall. A guard (morion helmet, buff leather jerkin) crouches at Nagoji's feet, unlocking the long bar that runs through the ankle irons of the whole row. Only the bar comes away. Nagoji's ankle cuffs stay on, now joined to each other by a short hobble chain about a forearm long.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He knew where I sat. He had spent too many hours standing over me.

copy.speaker: JOÃO
copy.text: On your feet, marata. The Viceroy has found a use for you.

panels.description: Nagoji halfway up from the floor, rising slowly: one bandaged hand braced flat on the wall, knees still bent, a wince held behind a set jaw. The hobble chain hangs between his bare ankles. João already turning away, uninterested.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My legs swung free, terrifyingly light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I forced myself not to limp.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Six men on one length of chain at the foot of the stair. Every man wears the same irons: a rigid hinged iron collar with a ring at the side, the one chain running collar to collar along the line; wrist manacles joined by a short slack chain; ankle cuffs joined by a short hobble chain. Nagoji in the foreground, three-quarter back view, his face in profile as he whispers. Two men ahead of him, seen from behind: Keshavrao. Keshavrao lock: about nineteen; beardless apart from a faint youthful moustache; a rounder, softer face than Nagoji's; narrow shoulders; black hair hacked short and ragged above the ears; faded grey-brown torn knee-length tunic, never ochre; no ear stud; thin unbandaged hands; no facial scar, no coat or vest. His head is turned a few degrees toward the whisper, shoulders gone rigid, eyes kept forward. His right hand hangs at his hip, fingers curled around an absent grip, the slack in his wrist chain letting it reach there, the left hand trailing with it. A Portuguese gaol guard (morion, buff leather jerkin, club in hand) walks alongside the line at the gap between the two men. The other four prisoners vary in age and build, in grey, brown and off-white rags.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Keshavrao. One of my riders.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (whisper)
copy.text: Rao.

panels.description: The chain of men climbing a turning stone stair, seen from below: iron collars, the one chain between them, hobbled ankles on the steps. The stone is black at the bottom of the frame and bleaches toward white at the top, where daylight waits.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The climb was like being born through a tunnel of stone.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Oil. Bread. Sea.

panels.description: Wide. A courtyard of whitewashed walls under a glaring sky, the whole frame burned almost to white so the glare hurts. The prisoners flinch and squint, raising chained hands against the light. Portuguese musketeers line the walls: broad hats tilted, buff leather coats, matchlock muskets, matchcords coiled at their belts. They must not read as British redcoats or Dutch blue-coats. Far across the yard, near the gate, tiny: Father Duarte, one thin black figure in a broad round travel hat.

Over Nagoji's shoulder (edge of his thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, loose curly hair), the chain shuffling past the gate. Duarte close now: broad round travel hat shading grey, tired eyes, a leather satchel over one shoulder, plain black cassock with a small cross, no white collar tab, scholar's stoop. His gaze has travelled the length of the chain and found Nagoji. Their eyes meet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Father Duarte. I expected triumph, or at least satisfaction.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The stubborn Maratha, broken at last.

panels.description: Tight on Duarte. His jaw has tightened. His ink-stained right hand is raised at his chest, partway through a small, slow sign of the cross toward the chain. His eyes show he did not plan it: the gesture escaped him almost before he knew it, and now he is completing it slowly and deliberately. This is not the quick ward against contamination; it is something he did not mean to show.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A blessing, perhaps. Or an apology.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Background: Duarte's back as he passes through a side door into the fortress, the door half shut behind him. Foreground: Nagoji's face in profile (clean-shaven chin with light stubble at most, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, no beard), still watching the door, the collar chain pulling him on.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I filed his face away in the part of my mind that kept accounts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men who hesitate are men who can be used.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Someday, I thought, that hesitation might matter.

panels.description: A narrow Goan street: lime-washed laterite houses with red tile roofs leaning inward, wooden balconies almost touching overhead, windows glazed with pale oyster-shell panes. Goan Catholics in clean cotton stepping aside, hands over their mouths and noses: men in European-cut coats and breeches, one holding a rosary, women in white veils. In two or three separate doorways stand Hindu merchants in white turbans, white angarkhas and gold earrings (a forehead mark is fine for them), faces carefully blank. The prisoners pass in the near foreground only as chained wrists and rag-clad backs, no faces.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Their eyes told a different story.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They weighed the value of the bodies in chains.

panels.description: Large, about two fifths of the page. The harbour. Masts clustered against the sky like a forest of stripped trees; gulls; ropes and water. One ship looms over the rest, hull black and high, her stern built up like a little fortress of carved wood and painted saints. No national flag: only plain white pennants at the mastheads; no green-and-red flag, no Dutch or British colours; no name or lettering anywhere on the hull or stern. On a wharf platform beneath her, a stout lay shipping clerk in a brown coat and a pale grey broad-brimmed felt hat checks a ledger against the lines of chained prisoners, the ledger held with its pages turned away from the viewer. He is clearly not in black and not a priest. Nagoji's chain small in the foreground, his ochre tunic the one warm note among grey and brown rags. Keep open sky at the top for lettering.

copy.speaker: PRISONER (behind)
copy.text: To Angola. Africa.

copy.speaker: OLD PRISONER
copy.text: Not this one. The Jesuits need bodies for their lands to the south.

copy.speaker: OLD PRISONER
copy.text: They will work us until we forget our own names.

panels.description: Low angle from the wharf, looking up the gangplank, slick with sea and tar, to the ship's rail. João stands on the wharf at the foot of the gangplank, seen side-on, yanking the chain toward it with both fists. The prisoners climb the flexing plank above him, and at the top a ship's hand in a shirt and head cloth takes the chain over. Inset in the lower corner, tight: Nagoji's bare feet with the ankle cuffs and the short hobble chain on a wet, flexing plank, a strip of dark water glinting through the gap below. João's balloon sits in the main frame; both captions sit in the inset.

copy.speaker: JOÃO
copy.text: Faster. The tide waits for no man. Not even maratas.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: An old, absurd thought.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Horses would hate this.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Compose on one axis. Nagoji in the foreground at the lip of an open hatch, a black square in the deck below him, looking back once over his shoulder. Beyond the rail, small and white: the town, the fortress, the hills. A Portuguese guard (morion, buff leather jerkin) at his back driving the chain toward the hatch. In the background only one or two free working sailors, African and Indian lascars in shirts and head cloths hauling a line, no irons. Canvas overhead. No flag, no lettering.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The world of land, with its forts and fields and familiar dust, already felt far away.

panels.description: Wide. The hold. Wooden shelves along both sides, divided into little pens by upright planks, four or five chained men seated in each, the prisoners in grey, brown and off-white rags. Every man wears a rigid hinged iron collar, chained wrist manacles and hobbled ankles. Iron rings are bolted into the beams overhead, each a little to one side of the pen it serves: the chain leaves each collar at the side, droops in a slack loop along the plank, then rises to its ring. No chain hangs taut and vertical above any head. A guard (morion, buff leather jerkin) carries the lantern away up the ladder; beyond him, far above, a small square of daylight shows at the top of the ladder. The dark closes in behind the lantern.
Insert, tight. The plank just above Nagoji's head, gouged with rough strokes, small crosses and circles, with no lines of script and no letters. His bandaged fingertips resting on them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Prayers, in a script I could not read.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Another prisoner, another ship, another journey that ended somewhere in chains.

panels.description: Close two-shot in the dark, faces a hand's width apart. Nagoji on the left (clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, long curly loose hair, ochre tunic). Keshavrao on the right (short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer younger face, grey-brown tunic, no scar), in the same pen by accident or indifference, has turned his head at last. Both in iron collars; one slack chain links both collars to the ring on the beam off to one side.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Sahib.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In camp I had insisted he use my name. We were both sons of the Deccan.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now there was comfort in the old military habit.

panels.description: Same two-shot, same sides: Nagoji left, Keshavrao right. Nagoji answering. Keshavrao bent in a small breathless laugh that has become a cough, narrow shoulders hunched against the collar, chained fists at his mouth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Rao. You are still alive.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: For now.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Their point of view, straight up through the hatch far above: a square of blue sky cut by strips of rigging. A gull crosses it, a white streak against the blue. No figures in frame. The balloon comes from off-panel below.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And the ship began to move.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO (off, below)
copy.text: Do you know where they send us?

panels.description: Two-shot in the pen, the hull now leaning gently with the swell. Nagoji on the left (clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, loose curly hair, ochre tunic), steady, answering. Keshavrao on the right (short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, no scar), low and bitter, eyes on the planks. Both in iron collars, chained wrist manacles and hobbled ankles; one slack chain links both collars to the ring on the beam off to one side.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: South. That much is certain.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: They need men to cut cane. Fields of sugar as tall as a man.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: We will sweat for their salvation.

panels.description: Keshavrao alone in the present (short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar and manacles, no scar), silent, head down, knees drawn up. Set into the corner as an inset with a soft, stained edge, the same treatment as the memory image in Chapter 1 panel 6.5: a warm-toned memory of Keshavrao near Chaul. The same young face with his hair uncut and loose to the shoulders, bareheaded, in a white angarkha with a sash and a sheathed sword at his hip, on a bay horse (not a black mare), mouth open in song. The Portuguese appear only as distant musket smoke behind him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Near Chaul he dared the Portuguese to shoot the song out of his mouth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The dungeon had scraped that away.

panels.description: Two-shot, same sides: Nagoji left (clean-shaven chin, thick moustache), Keshavrao right. Nagoji steady; Keshavrao half smiling for the first time, tired. Both in iron collars and chained manacles.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We are not there yet. As long as we move, there is a chance.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: The sahib still counts chances.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It is what I know.

panels.description: Wider, days later. The pen and the shelves beyond in dim grey light through a hatch grating. A wooden trough of rice and dried fish, a water cask, men coughing along the shelves, the weaker sagging against the stronger; the other prisoners in grey, brown and off-white rags. Nagoji and Keshavrao in their pen in the middle distance, Nagoji on the left, Keshavrao on the right, both in collars, manacles and hobbled ankles. The balloon comes down through the grating from off-panel above.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Time on a ship is different from time on land.

copy.speaker: SAILOR (above)
copy.text: Wind is with us. If it holds we round the cape before the worst of the storms.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, the tallest panel on the page. Up-angle through the open hatch: Portuguese sailors and an officer silhouetted against a bright sky, one leaning on the coaming, laughing. The sailors in shirts and head cloths; the officer in a tricorne hat, seen only in silhouette. Light pours down onto the upturned, sick faces in the hold, Nagoji's among them at the lower edge of the frame, lit, eyes narrowed. Leave the sky area clear for lettering.

copy.speaker: SAILOR 2 (above)
copy.text: This run is cursed. They say God sends warnings.

copy.speaker: OFFICER (above)
copy.text: God sends opportunity. These bodies are silver if they live.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He named a number of cruzados per head, as if we were sacks of pepper.

copy.speaker: OFFICER (above)
copy.text: Pray for their health, not their souls.

panels.description: The hatch shut again; near dark. The frame is canted a few degrees: a wooden dipper hanging from a peg on the upright plank hangs off true, and the water in the trough has slopped to one side. Keshavrao (short ragged hair, grey-brown tunic, no scar) shivering, knees drawn up, braced against the upright plank. Nagoji beside him on the left. Both in iron collars, chained wrist manacles and hobbled ankles; one slack chain links both collars to the ring on the beam off to one side.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: If there is a storm, will the ship break?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: All ships break. The question is when and how.

panels.description: Medium shot. Keshavrao seated, knees drawn up, face turned away, eyes toward the hull planks. His manacled right hand rests at his hip, fingers half-curled around a hilt that is not there; the slack wrist chain lets the left hand lie beside it. Iron collar with the slack chain as before. Short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, no scar.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO (quiet)
copy.text: If the chains break too, I will follow wherever you jump, sahib.

panels.description: Nagoji's face, close (clean-shaven chin with light stubble at most, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, loose curly hair, no beard). Nothing moves in it, but something heavy has arrived.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words settled over me heavier than iron.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had never meant to collect followers.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One boy's loyalty wrapped itself like a rope around my chest.

panels.description: Tight on hands. Nagoji's bandaged hand, entering from the left, resting across the narrow gap on Keshavrao's forearm. Keshavrao's thin, unbandaged fingers closed over it. Manacles and their short chains on both pairs of wrists.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If there is a chance, I will not leave you.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Neither of us mentioned that promises made in chains are the easiest to break.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Still in the hold: the storm is only heard and felt. The whole frame canted about ten degrees, clearly steeper than 6.1. A slack loop of spare chain swings well off true from a beam ring, attached to no one; the trough has slid against the upright. At the far end of the shelves a prisoner sits with his eyes shut and his lips moving in prayer. Grey light at a hatch seam overhead is broken by the shadow of running feet. In the foreground Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right) braced in their pen, Keshavrao's fingers still over Nagoji's bandaged hand. No exterior, no lightning, no sky.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Arabian Sea was beginning to remind us who owned this ship.
